findings.title: OptimizedCursorPaginator is not datetime-compatible but is used with order_by="-datetime"
findings.body: OptimizedCursorPaginator overrides get_item_key/value_from_cursor with the integer-key logic from Paginator. The new endpoint path in src/sentry/api/endpoints/organization_auditlogs.py (line 80) instantiates it with order_by="-datetime", so self.key is "datetime" and each item's value is a Python datetime. get_item_key then calls math.floor(datetime), which raises TypeError. Additionally, value_from_cursor returns the raw integer cursor value instead of converting it to a datetime like DateTimePaginator does, so any cursor with a value will compare a timestamp column to an integer in SQL and can fail with a Postgres operator error. The result is that any non-empty request with optimized_pagination=true by an eligible admin returns HTTP 500.

findings.title: Negative-offset path relies on unsupported negative Django QuerySet slicing
findings.body: When enable_advanced_features is true and cursor.offset is negative, the code sets start_offset = cursor.offset and then evaluates queryset[start_offset:stop] with a negative start. Django QuerySet slicing explicitly does not support negative indexing/slicing and raises ValueError/AssertionError (or otherwise generates invalid SQL OFFSET), so a crafted or generated negative cursor causes a 500. The adjacent comment claiming Django ORM handles negative slicing automatically is false. Additionally, the prev-page cleanup condition at line 891 compares len(results) to offset + limit + extra rather than to the number of rows actually fetched when start_offset differs from offset, so it would not correctly drop the extra row for negative offsets.
